08/200506 / Dc (Nw) In the matter of :
Sh. Satbir S/o Sh. Om Prakash R/o Village & Po Rani Khera, Delhi ....Petitioner Vs.
1. Union of India Through Land Acquisition Collector North West, Delhi
2. Delhi Development Authority Through Its Vice Chairman Ina Vikas Sadan, New
Delhi ....

Respondents Date of institution of the petition : 18.12.2012 Date of final
Arguments : 18.04.2023 Date of Decision : 18.04.2023

Appearance (s) :Shri J.S.
Antil, Ld. Counsel for the Petitioner Shri Sandeep Yadav, Ld. Counsel for R1/Union
of India.
Ms. Renu Gupta, Ld. Counsel for R2/Dda.

Shri Parveen, Sr. Asst. for Lac (Nw).
Notification U/S 4 of Land Acquisition Act F.11(19)/2001/L&B/La/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 Lac no.
156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/Dc(Nw)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 1 of 10 Notification
U/s 6 of Land Acquisition Act F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/La/28049 dt. 18.03.2004 Reference
Petition Under Section 18 Of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
J U D G M E N T

/ AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioner mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act

, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 Sh. Satbir vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63540606/
1 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), acquired situated in the revenue LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 10 estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees, tubewell and borings.

4. It is stated that the petitioner is the cobhumidhar and in possession of land bearing Khasra no.
39/6/2, 15/1, total admeasuring 02 bighas and 02 biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.
It is stated that the compensation awarded by the learned LAC is too low, unjust, arbitrary without any reasonable basis and the same is not acceptable to the petitioners.
The petitioners are recorded bhumidhars of the said land which has been acquired vide the said order.
The said land is very fertile and also gives handsome income to the petitioners in the form of 34 crops in a year.

6. It is stated that the said land is situated in village Rani Khera and is well connected with roads from all sides at the time of acquisition and was having great potential value for the residential as well as commercial LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 10 purposes.
The said land is duly levelled and as such gives handsome income to the petitioners.
7. It is stated that the said land is situated near NH10 and is having a great potential value as a perfect building/commercial site.

The building activities and commercial activities is coming up for last more than 15 years and, therefore, the said land has great potential value and the market value of the said land is more than Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

It is stated that all kind of civic amenities i.e. electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college were situated in and around the said land and the said land has great potential value.
8.

It is also stated that the said land is approachable by mettled roads and is very close to Mundka Industrial area which is fully developed at the time of issuance of the notification under Section 4 of the Act as adjoining areas situated in the vicinity of the said land have been developed as perfect industrial areas, therefore, the market value of the said land also requires to be assessed on the said basis.

There are many residential colonies in and around the said land, which shows the great potential value of said land at the time of passing of the notification under Section 4 of the Act and as such the said land could easily get Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

9. It is stated that the compensation assessed by the learned LAC is not based on the sound reasoning in as much as the said land has more LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 10 potential/market value which is not less than Rs. 10,000 per square yards.

The assessment done by the learned LAC is totally wrong and illegal Sh. Satbir vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63540606/
2 and the same should be rectified and compensation paid to the petitioners may be enhanced.
10. It is stated that the petitioner also claims for severance of the said land as per the process of law.
The petitioners are not in positions to cultivate his remaining land due to said acquisition.

11. It is stated that due to the excellent situation of the said land, high potentiality fertility of the said land, it is prayed that the petitioners may kindly be awarded the compensation of the land @ Rs.
10,000 per square yards along with solatium @30% and interest and other benefits.
12.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1/UOI and, it is, inter alia submitted that the present reference petition is not maintainable as petitioner have failed to led any evidence in respect of relief claimed.
The ld. LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land after taking into consideration the prevailing market rates at the time of passing of notification under section 4 of the Act.
The Award passed by the ld. LAC is just, legal, proper sufficient and reasonable.
All the other averments made in the present petition were denied in toto.
LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 10 13.

Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Rani Khera had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

14. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 10 15.
It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the DDA on 17.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same has been transferred to RPDVII on 17.10.2006.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action,
therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
Sh. Satbir vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63540606/
3 16.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 16.09.2014 :  ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?

OPP 2. Relief.
17.
Matter was listed for recording of petitioner's evidence.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 390 of 2016 Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.text: Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.

18. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 10 parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 19.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
20.

entities.text: State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 8 of 10 21.
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

22. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

Sh. Satbir vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63540606/
4 23.

entities.text: Satbir vs Union Of India on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioner is accordingly entitled to the same compensation for his land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
24. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the LAC no. 156 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Satbir v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 10 petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner RELIEF 25.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
26.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
Digitally  signed by  VIJAY VIJAY KUMAR ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT KUMAR DAHIYA

Date:
ON 18th DAY OF APRIL, 2023.
